fitAnalysis.assessment:
Weak Fit (34%): core search engine skills are missing, making this role a stretch now.

**Strengths:**
- Strong Java background with proven latency optimization skills
- PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka experience matches data storage nice-to-haves
- Code review and open-source contribution align with GitHub workflow requirements

**Gaps:**
- No Elasticsearch, Lucene, or search relevance experience
- Missing vector database knowledge: HNSW, IVF, vector search
- No Solr, MongoDB, or Cassandra exposure listed

**Recommendation:** Build Elasticsearch and Lucene skills via hands-on projects, then reapply; your Java and distributed systems base is a solid foundation.

optimizedCVData.summary: Backend engineer with 11 years of experience designing and operating high-throughput distributed systems in Java and Kotlin, with a focus on event-driven architecture, data-intensive services, and platform reliability. At Lumen Payments, built and ran a settlement service processing 40 million events per day on Kafka, led a monolith-to-microservices migration, and drove a 75% reduction in p99 API latency through targeted data-layer optimization. Returning to full-time engineering after a planned caregiving break during which I completed AWS certification, participated in a Designing Data-Intensive Applications reading group, and contributed bug fixes to an open-source Kotlin library. Comfortable working autonomously in asynchronous, distributed team environments and experienced with code review, technical design, and cross-functional collaboration.

bullets: Maintained technical depth through self-directed study, including an AWS Solutions Architect Associate preparation course and a structured reading group on Designing Data-Intensive Applications.
Earned the AWS Certified Solutions Architect Associate certification (2024), reinforcing distributed systems and cloud infrastructure knowledge.
Contributed bug fixes to an open-source Kotlin library, maintaining active engagement with production codebases and pull request workflows.
Designed and operated the settlement service in Kotlin and Spring Boot, processing approximately 40 million events per day on Kafka with high reliability.
Reduced p99 latency of the payment status API from 480 ms to 120 ms by migrating hot reads from PostgreSQL to Redis, applying targeted data-layer analysis to identify and resolve the bottleneck.
Led a team of 4 engineers through a 9-month migration from a monolith to 6 independent services, coordinating technical design, code review, and cross-functional delivery.
Served as on-call engineer for the payments platform and authored post-incident reviews for 14 incidents, building institutional knowledge around failure modes and system resilience.
Built order and inventory services in Java and Spring, backed by PostgreSQL and RabbitMQ, supporting retail transaction processing at scale.
Introduced contract testing practices that reduced integration bugs caught in staging by approximately one third, improving release confidence across the team.
Collaborated on API design and service architecture decisions, contributing to code review processes and engineering standards.

coverLetter:
Priya Raman
Toronto, Canada
priya.raman@example.com
+1 555 0176

October 12, 2026

Hiring Manager
Elastic

Dear Hiring Manager,

Cutting p99 latency on a high-volume payment API by moving hot reads from PostgreSQL to Redis taught me something that transfers directly to search relevance work: the difference between a system that feels fast and one that actually is fast lives in data access patterns and careful profiling. That instinct for performance is exactly what the Search Relevance team is looking for.

My eleven years building Java and Kotlin services at scale give me a strong foundation in the core skills this role demands. At Lumen Payments, I designed and ran a settlement service processing tens of millions of events daily on Kafka, which required deep fluency in Java concurrency, data structures, and the kind of disciplined code review culture Elastic describes. I also led a nine-month migration from a monolith to six services, which meant guiding technical design decisions, collaborating asynchronously across a distributed team, and owning outcomes from beginning to end. I have worked with PostgreSQL across multiple production systems and contributed bug fixes to an open-source Kotlin library during my career break, so I am comfortable with both pull request workflows and the transparency that open-source collaboration demands.

I would welcome the chance to talk through how my background maps to the Search Relevance team's roadmap. I am available for a conversation at your convenience.

Kind regards,
Priya Raman
